_what: The one number nobody was watching. Refresh it with a REAL measurement, never an estimate:
_how: git clone --bare --quiet https://github.com/paolosarn/bohemia b.git && cd b.git && git count-objects -vH
_why_not_measured_in_the_gate: a bare clone is ~54s and ~900MB of network; the suite runs the gate every ship. So the gate holds a RECORDED measurement and fails when it goes stale, rather than pretending it can compute the packed size cheaply. A local `git count-objects` is NOT a substitute: a working session accumulates loose objects (mine held 5.34 GiB of them against a 900 MB real repo) and reports a number 7x too big.
_growth_note: measured post-extraction (8/4 -> 8/6) on the real clone, packed bytes. The 7-day average is 65.6 MB/day but it includes the pre-extraction 38MB alpha versions, which delta-compressed unusually well and flatter the number. 32.5 is the honest current rate.
_limits_source: docs.github.com repository-limits: per-file 100 MB hard; repository 1 GB recommended ceiling; under 5 GB strongly recommended, above which GitHub makes contact and can restrict the repository.
